newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOTEX AGM CANCELS TWO 1997/98 BOND ISSUES.
newsitem.headline: FOTEX AGM CANCELS TWO 1997/98 BOND ISSUES.

text.p: Shareholders of Hungarian retail group Fotex Rt have cancelled two convertible bond issues to existing shareholders, planned for September 1997 and March 1998.

The two issues would have been the third and fourth in a series totalling a maximum $20 million of which the first two issues in November 1996 and March 1997 raised $2.536 million and $2.747 million, respectively.
Shareholders rejected the board's proposal that the timing of the bond issues be left at their discretion.

During the first two private issues, limited to existing foreign shareholders, Panama-registered Blackburn Inc., which has a stake of some 36 percent in Fotex, subscribed 313 bonds of 317 and during the second one 325 bonds out of 343.

The cancellation came after a debate in which minority shareholder Osterreichische Kontrollbank (OKB) expressed concern that Blackburn could acquire a majority if it uses the conversion option of bonds to shares.
"I simply cannot grasp why OKB did not subscribe more bonds," Fotex Chairman and CEO Gabor Varszegi said, adding that the company could fund its present expansion plans.
The three-year bonds bear an interest rate of between eight and 12 percent and owners have the option to convert them into shares one month ahead of the maturity.
